diagnosis.overall_diagnosis: The agent misclassified several solutions that stop route leaks but do not break the oscillation preference cycle. Specifically, it marked export-policy/no-export-community/ingress-filter/RPKI solutions as resolving both, when the test expects them to resolve only the route leak (oscillation_resolved=False). The skill needs sharper rules distinguishing which policy fixes break the preference cycle vs. which only stop leaks.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The skill's guidance conflates leak-stopping policies with cycle-breaking policies. The agent concluded that no-export community, export policy blocking provider routes to peer, and ingress filter on hub2 all resolve oscillation too, but per the verifier these only resolve the route leak. The skill lacks an explicit rule that oscillation resolution requires modifying the local-preference/routing-preference cycle itself (hub1's preference for hub2 or vice versa), not merely filtering advertisements. Export/ingress filters and communities change what is advertised/accepted but do not change the preference ordering that causes oscillation. Also, RPKI origin validation should resolve neither (origin is already correct), not route leak.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Add a precise classification rubric to azure-bgp/SKILL.md: (1) Oscillation is resolved ONLY by solutions that break the routing-preference cycle — i.e., changes to local-preference, routing preference hierarchy, routing intent (which overrides BGP path selection), UDR data-plane override, or export filters that remove the alternate path hub1 uses (routes learned from hub2 re-advertised). (2) Route leaks are resolved by solutions that stop hub1↔hub2 from exporting provider-learned routes to each other via Virtual WAN — including no-export community, export policy blocking provider routes to peer, and ingress filtering on the receiving hub rejecting AS_PATH containing provider ASN. (3) Explicitly state that no-export community, export-policy-blocking-provider-routes-to-peer, and ingress AS_PATH filters on the receiving hub resolve the route leak but do NOT by themselves break the preference cycle (oscillation_resolved=False), because the cycle is defined by local preference values, not by advertisement filtering. (4) Clarify that RPKI origin validation resolves neither oscillation nor route leak when the origin AS is already legitimate; it only addresses origin hijacks. (5) Reaffirm that only routing intent, UDR override, and preference/export-path changes that remove hub1's preferred path via hub2 resolve both.
